items.stem: What is gross domestic product (GDP)?
options: The value of exports minus imports
The total income of a country’s citizens wherever they live
The total value of output produced within a country in a year
items.answer: The total value of output produced within a country in a year
items.markingKey: Domestic: within borders, regardless of ownership.

items.stem: Explain why the output, income and expenditure methods of measuring national income should give the same result.
items.answer: The value of output produced is spent by buyers (expenditure) and that spending is paid out as incomes (wages, rent, interest, profit) to the factors that produced it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: output = expenditure; 1 mark: expenditure becomes income [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between GDP and GNI.
items.answer: GDP measures output produced within a country’s borders; GNI adds income earned abroad by residents and subtracts income paid to foreign residents (net primary income).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: The table shows data for Calvania. items.answer: $830 billion

items.answer: (a) GDP = $810bn; GNI = $825bn; NNI = $775bn. (b) They are redistributions of income, not payments for current output; including them would double count.

items.stem: Extract: Nominal GDP in Quentara rose from $800 billion to $880 billion, while the price level rose by 4% and the population by 1%. The government claims living standards have “risen sharply”. However, an estimated 30% of activity takes place in the informal economy and air pollution in Hanoi has worsened. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in nominal GDP. (b) Calculate real GDP in the second year in base-year prices. (c) Explain the difference between nominal and real GDP.
items.answer: (a) 10% (b) $846.2 billion (c) Nominal at current prices; real adjusted for inflation, shows volume of output.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: 10% [1] (b) 880 ÷ 1.04 [2] (c) Credit: Nominal at current prices; real adjusted for inflation, shows volume of output. [2]

items.answer: (a) 10% (b) Informal economy unrecorded; pollution and other externalities; distribution; population growth.

items.stem: How is gross national income (GNI) calculated from GDP?
options: GDP plus net primary income from abroad
items.answer: GDP plus net primary income from abroad
items.markingKey: GNI = GDP + income earned abroad by residents − income paid to foreigners.

items.stem: Explain why double counting must be avoided when measuring output.
items.answer: Counting intermediate goods and the final goods that contain them would overstate output; use value added or final goods only.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: problem; 1 mark: value added solution [2]

items.stem: Many workers from Pelora work abroad and send income home, while foreign firms in Pelora send profits overseas. Explain how this affects the difference between Pelora’s GDP and GNI.
items.answer: Income earned abroad by residents adds to GNI; profits paid to foreign owners are subtracted. GNI exceeds GDP if inflows are larger than outflows.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inflows add; 1 mark: outflows subtract [2]

items.answer: $920 billion

items.stem: Extract: Nominal GDP in Halvoria rose from $300 billion to $342 billion, while the price level rose by 6% and the population by 1%. The government claims living standards have “risen sharply”. However, an estimated 30% of activity takes place in the informal economy and air pollution in Jakarta has worsened. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in nominal GDP. (b) Explain the difference between nominal and real GDP.
items.answer: (a) 14% (b) Nominal at current prices; real adjusted for inflation, shows volume of output.

items.stem: What is real GDP?
options: GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
items.answer: GDP adjusted for changes in the price level
items.markingKey: Real = nominal ÷ price index × 100.

items.stem: Explain why economists use real rather than nominal GDP to measure economic growth.
items.answer: Nominal GDP can rise just because prices rise; real GDP removes the effect of inflation, so it shows changes in the volume of output.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: nominal includes price changes; 1 mark: real shows volume [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between GDP at market prices and GDP at basic prices.
items.answer: Market prices include indirect taxes and exclude subsidies paid; basic prices remove indirect taxes and add subsidies, showing the value received by producers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.answer: (a) Real GDP $522.7bn; growth +4.5%. (b) $25,000 → $25,623.89; +2.5%. (c) Average material living standards rose, though GDP per capita ignores distribution and non-market factors.

It is adjusted for population size
It is measured in real terms

items.stem: During a class discussion Sofia said: ‘A country with a higher GDP than another must have higher living standards.’ Explain what is wrong with this claim.
items.answer: Total GDP ignores population, price levels, distribution and non-market factors; GDP per capita at PPP is a better but still imperfect guide.
